column4: We downed our drinks and got out of there when the fight started.

column4: Brian drinks like a fish! I can't keep up with that guy!

column4: You can't handle your drink; stick to sparkling water.

column4: He always ends up throwing up on a night out: he just can't handle his drink.

column4: You need to pace yourself, you know you can't handle your drink!

column4: I think you might have a drinking problem. Have you thought about seeking help?

column4: He always seems to be having a drink to let off some steam, I think he might have a drinking problem.

column3: Muchas estrellas del rock recurren a los atracones en lugar de a las drogas.
column4: A lot of rock stars turn to binge-eating instead of drugs.

column3: Has adquirido el hábito de atiborrarte; tienes que salir de ese círculo vicioso.
column4: You've got into the habit of binge-eating; you need to break that vicious cycle.

column4: Binge-drinking is common among people in their early twenties in the UK and the US.

column3: Algunas personas comen en exceso cuando tienen problemas, mientras que otras simplemente dejan de comer por completo.
column4: Some people overeat when they have problems, whereas others just stop eating altogether.

column3: Si comes en exceso en Navidades, tendrás que quemarlo en enero.
column4: If you overeat over Christmas, you have to work it off in January.

column4: I got into the habit of overeating and it took me months to shift the weight I'd put on.

column3: Me di un atracón que te mueres anoche y hoy me encuentro fatal.
column4: I stuffed myself silly last night and today I'm suffering big-time.

column4: He always stuffs himself silly at parties, and then he normally ends up feeling ill.

column4: A lot of people stuff their faces with all kinds of junk food just out of sheer boredom.

column4: Are we out of snacks? Yup, we gobbled them all up over the weekend.

column4: He gobbled the whole pie up. It must've been good!

column4: Your cousin gobbled it all down in five minutes! Hurry up or you'll not get any dessert.

column4: After three months of dieting, she caved in and wolfed down a whole cake. Poor thing, she feels awful now.

column3: Soy muy estricto con mi dieta, pero una vez a la semana me permito engullir una pizza entera.
column4: I'm really strict with my diet, but once a week I allow myself to wolf down a whole pizza.

column3: Él engulló su comida y se fue sin pagar.
column4: He wolfed down his food and left without paying.

column3: Esto es algo en lo que pensar: si se cae un árbol y no hay nadie para oírlo, ¿hace ruido?
column4: Here's some food for thought: if a tree falls and no one is around to hear it, does it make a sound?

column3: Tartas en forma de políticos famosos... ¡eso sí que es algo en lo que pensar!
column4: Cakes in the shape of famous politicians... now there's some food for thought!

column3: Esto es algo en lo que pensar: ¿es mejor haber amado y perdido, o no haber amado nunca?
column4: Here's some food for thought: is it better to have loved and lost or to never have loved at all?

column3: Me estoy muriendo de hambre, ¡me comería un buey!
column4: I'm starving, I could eat a horse!

column4: I could eat a horse right now. Let's just go into the first place we find.

column4: If you're so hungry that you could eat a horse, then let's order the mixed grill, it's absolutely massive!

column4: Put your wallet away sunshine, the drinks are on me!

column4: No, no, put your money away. It's on the house.

column4: I know you're broke so this one's my treat.

column4: Whereas the German teacher commands no respect whatsoever, the Russian teacher has all her students eating out of the palm of her hand.

column4: He's happily married but he also wants to play the field; he can't have his cake and eat it!

column4: She thinks she deserves the promotion but she's not prepared to put in more hours. She can't have her cake and eat it.

column4: I can't believe that lodger! He's eating us out of house and home!

column4: I'll eat my hat if you win the race!

column4: If it turns out you're right, I'll eat my hat!

column4: If the contract goes to KMPJ Ltd, I swear I'll eat my hat!

column4: I said I'd never smoke again, but I guess I'll have to eat my words now.

column4: He said he'd never go back to her, but he's eaten his words, hasn't he?

column4: Craig told us he'd get the job. He has to eat his words now!

column4: He kept on boasting about how good he was, but in the end, when he was defeated, he had to eat humble pie.

column4: He's going to have to eat humble pie now! It tastes bitter, doesn't it?

column4: When everyone went on strike, he had to eat humble pie and admit he wasn't a perfect boss.
